title: Caramelised Onion Soup with Gruyère Toasts
summary: A deeply savoury soup of slowly caramelised onions simmered in beef stock with thyme, topped with golden baguette toasts and bubbling Gruyère.
equipment: large heavy-based pot or casserole with a lid (at least 5 litres)

ingredients.item: yellow onions (about 6 large), halved and thinly sliced
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Soften the onions
steps.text: Melt the butter in the pot over medium-high heat, then add the onions, salt and sugar. Cover and cook for 15-20 min, stirring every few minutes, until the onions have collapsed and released their liquid. The lid traps steam, which wilts the onions quickly before browning begins.

steps.title: Caramelise slowly
steps.text: Take off the lid, lower the heat to medium and cook for 35-45 min more, stirring every 3-4 min and scraping the brown film from the bottom. The onions are ready when deep golden-brown and jammy. If they start to catch, add 2 tbsp water and scrape; that brown film is concentrated sugar and flavour, so you want it back in the onions, not burnt.

steps.title: Add flour and stock
steps.text: Stir in the flour for 1 min, then pour in 250 ml of the stock and scrape the bottom clean. Add the rest of the stock with the water, thyme, bay leaf and pepper. Bring to the boil and simmer uncovered for 20 min; the flour gives the broth a little body.

steps.title: Season and brighten
steps.text: Lift out the thyme stalks and bay leaf, then stir in the lemon juice. A touch of acid balances the sweetness of the caramelised onions.

steps.title: Toast the bread
steps.text: Meanwhile, heat the oven grill (broiler) to high. Toast the baguette slices on the tray under the grill for 1-2 min per side until dry and golden. Dry toasts float on the soup and hold up under the cheese rather than going soggy straight away.

steps.title: Gratinate and serve
steps.text: Set the bowls on the tray, ladle in the boiling-hot soup and float 2 toasts on each, then cover with the cheese. Grill for 3-5 min until the cheese is melted, bubbling and browned in spots. The bowls will be very hot, so lift them with oven gloves and serve on plates.

tips: A common mistake is rushing the caramelising with high heat; the onions burn outside before turning sweet, so keep to medium and be patient.
Scrape the base of the pot every few minutes, as the brown film is where much of the flavour lives.
Use ovenproof bowls only, and keep the soup boiling hot when you ladle it so the cheese melts evenly.
storage: Cool the soup without the toasts, refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat until boiling hot (74°C), then add fresh toasts and cheese.
